provenance: Batch b10: the proofs al-Mughnī and its peers cite for each position, weighed by an agent under docs/architecture/taarud-reconciliation.md §redesign (tiers per Rawḍa v02 p389–390, murajjiḥāt per Rawḍa and al-Kawkab); every excerpt located verbatim; qaṭʿī and ijmāʿ tiers reviewed. No human review yet.

proofs.dalil: Rationale: divorce and the ḥadd of qadhf are two rights against him; both follow from the one utterance, and his word is not accepted to drop either.
proofs.excerpt_ar: وبه جزم في عمد الأدلة أنه يحد ; لأنهما حقان عليه
proofs.note: Ibn ʿAqīl's first possibility, the one asserted in ʿUmad al-Adilla. No listed work treats the masʾala; Ibn Rajab's report is the only argument found. Qiyas.

proofs.dalil: Rationale: qadhf and divorce exclude each other, so once the word is taken as divorce it cannot also be qadhf.
proofs.excerpt_ar: والثاني : لا يحد لأنه لو كان قذفا لم يكن طلاقا لتنافيهما
proofs.note: Ibn ʿAqīl's second possibility (no ḥadd). A stated rationale: qiyas.

proofs.dalil: Qiyās: wuḍūʾ from one of two confused vessels, later found to be the ṭahūr one, is like praying before knowing the time has entered and then finding it had: the act was done without the knowledge its validity needs (aṣl: prayer before knowing the time; ʿilla: performing while the condition is not known).
proofs.excerpt_ar: لم يصح وضوءه) كما لو صلى قبل أن يعلم دخول الوقت فصادفه، وظاهره سواء تحرى أو لا
proofs.note: Cited by al-Buhūtī for the madhhab ruling (not valid) on exactly these facts: no ghalaba (no taḥarrī) and no presumption to build on. A stated analogy: qiyas.

proofs.dalil: Rationale for Abū al-Ḥusayn: firm certainty that the wuḍūʾ is valid is not a condition of it, so it stands once the water proves ṭahūr.
proofs.excerpt_ar: وقال القاضي أبو الحسين يصح وهو يرجع إلى أن الجزم بصحة الوضوء لا يشترط
proofs.note: Ibn Rajab gives this as the ground of Abū al-Ḥusayn's view (validity). A stated rationale, not a text: qiyas. None of the listed works argues for this view; al-Mubdiʿ (v01:p043) only reports it.

proofs.dalil: Rationale: the suspended intention («the farḍ if I am in ḥadath / if the time has entered, else renewal or nafl») only states what the act's ruling would be anyway without it, so voicing it does no harm.
proofs.excerpt_ar: فذكر ابن عقيل أنه يجزئه لأن هذا حكمه ولو لم ينوه، فإذا نواه لم يضره
proofs.note: Ibn ʿAqīl's ground for sufficiency; the prayer rests on a preponderant belief that the time has entered, which suffices. A stated rationale: qiyas.

proofs.dalil: Takhrīj a fortiori from Abū Bakr's view in the zakāt case (the hesitant intention does not suffice, «لم يخلص النية عن الفرض»): here even more so, since the zakāt case at least rested on a presumption of continuance and this one does not.
proofs.excerpt_ar: ويتخرج منه وجه في التي قبلها أنه لا يصح وأولى لأن هناك لم يبن على أصل مستصحب
proofs.note: The extracted wajh for insufficiency is a qiyās (awlā) from the following farʿ; Ibn Rajab himself notes it is answered by ghalabat al-ẓann on the time. Qiyas.

rebuttal.excerpt_ar: ويتخرج منه وجه في التي قبلها أنه لا يصح وأولى لأن هناك لم يبن على أصل مستصحب ولكنه بنى على غلبة ظن بدخول الوقت وهو يكفي في صحة الصلاة
rebuttal.note: Right after stating the a fortiori takhrīj, Ibn Rajab answers it. The prayer case rests on a probable belief that the time has begun, and that suffices for validity, so the a fortiori fails.

proofs.dalil: Rationale: he made the intention purely for the farḍ and only ordered the nafl after it; that is the payment's ruling even if unsaid (if the wealth had perished it would be voluntary), so saying it does not harm.
proofs.excerpt_ar: فبان سالما، أجزأت نيته؛ لأنه أخلص النية للفرض، ثم رتب عليها النفل، وهذا حكمها كما لو لم يقله
proofs.note: Ibn Qudāma's reason for sufficiency when the absent wealth proves safe. A stated rationale: qiyas.

proofs.dalil: Istiṣḥāb: the absent wealth is presumed to remain, so an intention to pay its zakāt despite doubt over its safety is valid.
proofs.excerpt_ar: جاز له إخراج الزكاة عنه، وكانت نية الإخراج صحيحة؛ لأن الأصل بقاؤه
proofs.note: This is the presumption that distinguishes the case (asl_mustashab): the intention is built on the continuance of the wealth. The original state: istishab.

proofs.dalil: Rationale for Abū Bakr: the intention was not made purely for the obligatory zakāt but hesitated between it and a voluntary gift.
proofs.excerpt_ar: وقال أبو بكر: لا يجزئه؛ لأنه لم يخلص النية للفرض
proofs.note: al-Mubdiʿ attaches Abū Bakr's denial to this very conditional formula («إن كان سالما ... وإلا فنفل»); in al-Mughnī the same reason is given for «زكاة مالي الغائب أو تطوع». A stated rationale: qiyas.

proofs.dalil: Rationale: on the riwāya that Ramaḍān needs a specified intention, this intention did not specify the fast as Ramaḍān's with firmness.
proofs.excerpt_ar: وإلا فهو نفل. لم يجزئه، على الرواية الأولى؛ لأنه لم يعين الصوم من رمضان جزما
proofs.note: Ibn Qudāma's ground for insufficiency, resting on the requirement of taʿyīn (the mashhūr). A stated rationale: qiyas.

proofs.dalil: Rationale: intention is firm resolve; a suspended intention is not firm.
proofs.excerpt_ar: ولا يصح عند من أوجبه؛ لأنه لم يجزم به والنية عزم جازم
proofs.note: al-Kāfī's reason for the same ruling on the same formula («فهو فرض وإلا فهو نفل»). Qiyas.

proofs.dalil: Rationale for Ṣāliḥ's report: under cloud the fast of that day is (on that riwāya) obligatory, so the hesitant intention suffices then, unlike a clear night.
proofs.excerpt_ar: ونقل صالح : أنه يصح بالنية المترددة والمطلقة مع الغيم دون الصحو؛ لوجوب صومه
proofs.note: al-Mubdiʿ gives Ṣāliḥ's report with its reason. A stated rationale: qiyas.

proofs.dalil: Rationale on the riwāya that taʿyīn is not required for Ramaḍān: he intended the fast, and that intention suffices.
proofs.excerpt_ar: صح عند من لم يوجب التعيين؛ لأنه نوى الصوم ونيته كافية
proofs.note: Cited for sufficiency on the same formula, on the riwāya on which Ṣāliḥ's report is built (al-Inṣāf v03:p295). Qiyas.

proofs.dalil: Istiṣḥāb: the deposited dinar is presumed to remain, so the exchange may be built on it under doubt; doubt does not remove certainty.
proofs.excerpt_ar: ووجه الأول، أن الأصل بقاؤه، فصح البناء عليه عند الشك، فإن الشك لا يزيل اليقين
proofs.note: Ibn Qudāma's argument for Ibn ʿAqīl's view (valid). The original state: istishab.

proofs.dalil: Qiyās on the sale of an absent animal whose life is doubted, which is valid and void only if it proves to have perished at the contract.
proofs.excerpt_ar: ولذلك صح بيع الحيوان الغائب المشكوك في حياته، فإن تبين أنه كان تالفا حين العقد
proofs.note: Same passage, for the same view; aṣl the absent animal, ʿilla a doubted existence presumed to continue. Qiyas.

proofs.dalil: Rationale for al-Qāḍī: the dinar is not known to remain, and ṣarf needs a present, known countervalue.
proofs.excerpt_ar: وقال القاضي: لا يصح؛ لأنه غير معلوم البقاء. وهو منصوص الشافعي
proofs.note: Given for al-Qāḍī's view (not valid), also al-Shāfiʿī's naṣṣ. A stated rationale: qiyas.

proofs.dalil: Rationale: the judge and his trustee are provided for from the treasury, so they need not take from the ward's property.
proofs.excerpt_ar: وأما الحاكم وأمينه فلا يأكلان شيئا لأنهما يستغنيان بمالهما في بيت المال
proofs.note: al-Buhūtī's reason for excluding them (the Iqnāʿ/Muntahā ruling). A stated rationale: qiyas.

proofs.dalil: Farq: the father may fix a fee for his executor even when a volunteer exists, so the executor acts by his permission; the judge may not pay anyone when a volunteer exists, so his trustee is unlike the executor.
proofs.excerpt_ar: وفرق بينه وبين الوصي بأن الأب له أن يجعل للوصي جعلا مع وجود متبرع
proofs.note: al-Qāḍī's first view, distinguishing the ḥākim's trustee from the testamentary executor. A stated rationale: qiyas.

proofs.dalil: Qiyās on the father's executor, taken from Aḥmad's naṣṣ that the judge takes a wage for judging in proportion to his work: so he may take for his work on the orphan's property.
proofs.excerpt_ar: وقال مرة: له الأكل كوصي الأب وأخذه من نص أحمد على أن الحاكم يأخذ على القضاء أجرا بقدر شغله
proofs.note: al-Qāḍī's second view, which al-Mardāwī calls «الصواب». A takhrīj and analogy: qiyas.

proofs.dalil: Qiyās on the executor/guardian: the waqf administrator is equal to him in meaning and ruling.
proofs.excerpt_ar: ويأكل ناظر وقف بمعروف نصا إذا لم يشترط الواقف له شيئا) لأنه يساوي الوصي معنى وحكما
proofs.note: al-Buhūtī's reason for the naṣṣ that the nāẓir eats where the founder stipulated nothing. Qiyas.

proofs.dalil: Qiyās on the zakāt collector, who takes for his work even when rich.
proofs.excerpt_ar: يحتج أكل) منه (بمعروف) إلحاقا له بعامل الزكاة
proofs.note: Sharḥ al-Muntahā's reason for the nāẓir eating without need and without a stipulation. Qiyas.

proofs.dalil: ʿUmar's waqf, entrusted to Ḥafṣa, in which he stipulated that its administrator may eat from it «بالمعروف»: Aḥmad drew from it that the administrator eats when that is stipulated, so (by mafhūm) not without it.
proofs.excerpt_ar: ونقل الميموني عن أحمد أنه ذكر حديث عمر حين وقف فأوصى إلى حفصة ثم قال أحمد: وليه يأكل منه بالمعروف إذا اشترط ذلك
proofs.note: The ṣaḥābī's own stipulation in his waqf, with no ṣaḥābī reported against it, read by Aḥmad as making the stipulation the ground of eating. fatwaSahabi; the denial rests on the mafhūm of Aḥmad's wording, which Ibn Rajab draws out.

proofs.dalil: Rationale: the agent and the hired worker can get their pay from the principal or hirer, so they have no need to eat from the property; the hired worker has already taken a wage for his work.
proofs.excerpt_ar: ومنها الوكيل والأجير والمعروف منعهما من الأكل لاستغنائهما عنه بطلب الأجرة من المؤجر والموكل
proofs.note: The stated ground of al-maʿrūf (they do not eat). A stated rationale: qiyas.

proofs.dalil: Farq: the agent can agree a fee with his principal; the executor cannot (the principal is dead), so the executor eats and the agent does not.
proofs.excerpt_ar: لأنه يمكنه موافقة الموكل على الأجرة، بخلاف الوصي أشار إليه القاضي
proofs.note: Given in Kashshāf for the agent for distributing alms; the same farq is reported by al-Inṣāf (v05:p341) for the agent generally. Qiyas.

proofs.dalil: Aḥmad (Ḥanbal) let the guardian and executor eat «because they are like the hired worker and the agent», which presupposes that the agent too may take for his upkeep.
proofs.excerpt_ar: يأكلان بالمعروف. لأنهما كالأجير والوكيل. وظاهر هذا: النفقة للوكيل
proofs.note: Not a sharʿī proof of its own but an inference from the imām's analogy (the agent as aṣl), drawn by al-Qāḍī; recorded as the only stated ground for this position. Qiyas.

proofs.dalil: Ḥadīth of Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, marfūʿ: «If you come to the wall of a garden, call the owner; if he answers [ask], otherwise eat without causing damage» (Aḥmad, Ibn Mājah; its men trustworthy).
proofs.excerpt_ar: فإن أجابك وإلا فكل من غير أن تفسد» رواه أحمد وابن ماجه ورجاله ثقات
proofs.note: Cited for eating from unguarded fruit with no condition of need. Connected marfūʿ āḥād: zanni.

proofs.dalil: Anas b. Mālik, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Samura and Abū Barza ate from fruit they passed; ʿUmar: «he eats and does not take a bundle»; Ibn ʿAbbās likewise.
proofs.excerpt_ar: أنه يأكل ولا يحمل، لما روي عن أبي زينب، قال: سافرت مع أنس بن مالك
proofs.note: al-Kāfī's proof for the first riwāya (eat, not carry). al-Mughnī (v09:p417) adds «قول من سمينا من الصحابة من غير مخالف، فيكون إجماعا» and answers Saʿd's abstaining as not a disagreement; a tacit consensus of ṣaḥāba, so fatwaSahabi, not ijma.

proofs.dalil: Ḥadīth of ʿAmr b. Shuʿayb from his father from his grandfather, marfūʿ, on hanging fruit: «Whatever one in need takes with his mouth, not taking a bundle, there is nothing on him; whoever carries some off owes twice its value and punishment» (graded ḥasan).
proofs.excerpt_ar: والثالثة: له الأكل إن كان جائعا، ولا يأكل إن لم يكن جائعا، لما روى عمرو بن شعيب
proofs.note: Cited in al-Kāfī for the riwāya that he eats only if hungry: the ḥadīth's qualifier «من ذي حاجة». Connected marfūʿ āḥād: zanni.

proofs.dalil: Ḥadīth of Rāfiʿ (b. ʿAmr): the Prophet said to him «Do not throw at it; eat what has fallen» (graded ṣaḥīḥ in al-Kāfī; al-Tirmidhī ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ in al-Mughnī).
proofs.excerpt_ar: والثانية: يباح ما سقط، ولا يرمي بحجر ولا يضرب، لما روى رافع
proofs.note: Cited in al-Kāfī for the riwāya that only fallen fruit is permitted. Connected marfūʿ āḥād: zanni.

proofs.dalil: Rationale: the two witnesses caused the taking of his property, so they are liable for what perished or cannot be recovered.
proofs.excerpt_ar: فله تضمين الشاهدين لأنهما سبب الاستيلاء عليه
proofs.who: Shams al-Dīn Ibn Qudāma, al-Sharḥ al-Kabīr
proofs.note: al-Sharḥ al-Kabīr for the man who returns alive after his death was testified to and his estate divided. Causation as ʿilla: qiyas.

proofs.dalil: Rationale: the property perished through their testimony.
proofs.excerpt_ar: البينة) التي شهدت بوفاته (ما تلف من ماله) لتلفه بسبب شهادتها
proofs.note: Sharḥ al-Muntahā for the Muntahā's ruling that the witnesses are liable. Qiyas.

proofs.dalil: Rationale: the direct taker (the heir who consumed it) is liable before the one who caused it; the witnesses only if he cannot be made to pay.
proofs.excerpt_ar: قلت: إن تعذر تضمين المباشر وإلا فالضمان عليه ; لأنه مقدم على المتسبب
proofs.note: al-Buhūtī's own qualification supports making the heirs pay first, as in al-Qāḍī's iḥtimāl; Ibn Rajab adds that they then recover from the witnesses «لتغريرهم». A stated rationale: qiyas.

proofs.dalil: Rationale: whoever consumed the property destroyed it without the owner's permission, so the owner may claim from him.
proofs.excerpt_ar: وللمالك تضمين المتلف لأنه أتلف ماله بغير إذنه
proofs.who: Shams al-Dīn Ibn Qudāma, al-Sharḥ al-Kabīr
proofs.note: al-Sharḥ al-Kabīr, same passage: the returning owner may also claim from the heir who consumed it. Qiyas.

proofs.dalil: Rationale: the executor is excused, not having known of the creditor.
proofs.excerpt_ar: دين يستغرقه) أي الثلث لاستغراقه جميع المال لم يضمن. لأنه معذور بعدم علمه رب الدين
proofs.note: Sharḥ al-Muntahā for no liability when an estate-consuming debt appears after he distributed the third. A stated rationale: qiyas.

proofs.dalil: Rationale for liability: the creditors' right attaches strongly to the estate (Aḥmad: «the estate belongs to the creditors, not the heirs»), so disposing of it against that right is answerable.
proofs.excerpt_ar: ولكنه تعلق قوي لا سيما إن قلنا لم ينتقل إلى الورثة ولهذا قال أحمد في رواية ابن منصور في التركة هي للغرماء
proofs.note: Ibn Rajab's statement of the ground of the riwāya of liability. A stated rationale resting on Aḥmad's naṣṣ: qiyas.

proofs.dalil: Rationale: the executor (or judge) is excused, not having known the legatee.
proofs.excerpt_ar: ثم ثبت) الموصى له (لم يضمن) موصى إليه ولا حاكم شيئا أي لأنه معذور بعدم علمه به
proofs.note: Sharḥ al-Muntahā for no liability after spending a bequest to an unknown legatee who then proves it. A stated rationale: qiyas.

proofs.dalil: Rationale from Aḥmad's naṣṣ: the estate is the creditors' before the heirs', so the heirs may dispose of it only on condition of liability.
proofs.excerpt_ar: هي للغرماء لا للورثة ولهذا لا يملك الورثة التصرف فيها إلا بشرط الضمان
proofs.note: Ibn Rajab states it in the executor's case and expressly of the heirs; it is the ground that separates them from the executor and makes them liable to the creditors (al-Qāḍī and Ibn ʿAqīl). Qiyas.

proofs.dalil: Takhrīj by analogy on the executor who distributed the third and is not liable when a consuming debt appears.
proofs.excerpt_ar: فإنهم يضمنون للغرماء ذكره القاضي وابن عقيل ويتخرج فيه وجه آخر بانتفاء الضمان من مسألة الوصي
proofs.note: Ibn Rajab's extracted wajh; aṣl the executor's case, carried over to the heirs executing the bequest. Qiyas.

proofs.dalil: Qiyās: the three attributes are all found in him, so it is as if she saw three men bearing the three attributes; each suspension is met.
proofs.excerpt_ar: فرأت رجلا أسود فقيها - طلقت ثلاثا) لوجود الصفات الثلاث فيه، أشبه ما لو رأت ثلاثة فيهم الثلاث صفات
proofs.note: al-Mubdiʿ (and al-Sharḥ al-Kabīr, Kashshāf) for the madhhab ruling of three divorces. Qiyas.

proofs.dalil: Rationale: the divorce is suspended on each attribute separately and each has occurred, as if found in three persons.
proofs.excerpt_ar: لأن الطلاق معلق على كل من هذه الصفات وقد وجدت أشبه ما لو وجدت في ثلاثة أعيان
proofs.note: Sharḥ al-Muntahā for the same ruling. Qiyas.

proofs.dalil: Rationale from the swearer's evident meaning: he meant «you are divorced» whichever attribute is met, so the unqualified wording is taken in that sense, it being the customary usage, unless he intends otherwise.
proofs.excerpt_ar: لأن الأظهر من مراد الحالف أنت طالق سواء ولدت ذكرا أو أنثى، وسواء كلمت رجلا أو فقيها أو أسود
proofs.note: Taqī al-Dīn's ground for one divorce only. A linguistic and customary rationale: qiyas.
